subject: Proposed 'Data Bridge' for Short-term Restore & Log Retention Exceptions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: security@healthsync.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 'Data Bridge' for short-term restore & log retention exception

Hi Sam and team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, HealthSync needs a short-term ability to restore customer data from backups created within a 60‑day window for recent incidents, while also maintaining our standard purge schedule. To balance that with our policy constraints and subprocessors, I've sketched a lightweight approach we’re calling a "Data Bridge":

- Purpose: temporary, encrypted replication of a narrow dataset into an EU restore-only bucket for up to 90 days when a legal/operational restore request is approved.
- Scope: only the minimum objects required for the restore (customer id + conversational blobs + minimal metadata). No profile KMs or broader telemetry.
- Controls: access tokens scoped, KMS-protected keys per-account, audit logs exported to immutable archive, and automated teardown after the approved window.

Attachments: data-bridge-sketch.png (high level), backup-retention-matrix.xlsx (proposed windows). I’ve also attached a DPA addendum draft (dpa-addendum_v0.3.pdf) with two clauses: (1) temporary cross-border replicate limited to approved restores, and (2) log retention exception flow & approvals.

Questions for your team:
1) Are the proposed controls sufficient for HealthSync's legal team to sign off on a short-term replicate?
2) Any mandatory subprocessor notices we need to surface (we are proposing a limited EU subprocessor for the bridge)?
3) Do you prefer the restore window to be 60 or 90 days (we recommended 90 for operational flexibility)?

Kimberly — tagging you for DPA / subprocessor language and for confirmation on whether the bridge approach triggers any SOC2 scope change.

Laura — can you confirm procurement timelines and whether a contract amendment runway of ~3 weeks is OK for this customer?

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Manager, Enterprise Sales (Retention & Compliance)
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198


From: Sam Carter <security@healthsync.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com, procurement@medtechco.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Data Bridge' for short-term restore & log retention exception

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the sketch — this helps a lot. A few clarifying points from HealthSync security/legal: 

- We need confirmation that the bridge data will be encrypted at rest with separate CMKs per customer and that key access is auditable (logs retained for at least 2 years).
- The EU subprocessor: we require a list of subprocessors and their locations up front. If the bridge provider is a new subprocessor, we’ll need written confirmation that they will only process data for the explicit restore and not index or use for ML training.
- Log retention: can Redwood provide an exception workflow that includes an internal audit step and a signed approval from HealthSync legal before the bridge is instantiated?

On timing — legal prefers a 60‑day replicate window as the default, with an option to extend to 90 days by written exception. That minimizes exposure.

Can Kimberley/Kim review the DPA addendum and confirm if the language is acceptable? Also looping in Acme Health legal since they have overlapping requirements for cross-border restores.

Thanks,
Sam
Security Lead, HealthSync
security@healthsync.com

On Tue, Aug 25, 2026 at 09:12 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (original message)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Carter <security@healthsync.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Data Bridge' for short-term restore & log retention exception

Thanks for the clear ask, Stephanie and Sam. A few notes from Legal & Security at Redwood: 

1) DPA addendum: the draft you sent is a good start. We will tighten the subprocessor clause to require (a) pre-approval for any new subprocessor engaged for the bridge, (b) a commitment that data is NOT used for training or analytics, and (c) contractual audit rights for HealthSync. I’ll incorporate those and circulate v0.4 by EOD.

2) Key management & logs: We can provision per-customer CMKs in the EU region and export key-access logs to an immutable archive with a 2-year retention. That will require a brief KMS onboarding step for accounts electing the bridge (we can automate with a template).

3) Exception flow: propose the following minimal workflow — (i) HealthSync submits a Restore Request Form (link in attachments), (ii) Redwood Security performs a scoped review, (iii) HealthSync legal signs approval, (iv) bridge is instantiated for up to 60 days and can be extended to 90 days with documented justification and signoff. We will record every step in the console and lock down RBAC.

Aditya — please confirm operational impact (capacity, expected storage, and snapshot immutability).

Sam — if HealthSync insists on 60 days by default, we are ok with that as long as the extension path exists. I’ll update the doc.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Carter <security@healthsync.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Data Bridge' for short-term restore & log retention exception

Hi all,

Procurement side — quick update: we can do a 3-week contract amendment runway if HealthSync returns the signed DPA addendum within 7 business days. I attached the backup-retention-matrix.xlsx with proposed timelines and estimated costs for the bridge (storage + minimal EU egress for restores).

Operational notes from Aditya (cc’d): estimated incremental storage for a typical HealthSync customer is ~12–30 GB per bridge instance, depending on conversation volume. The bridge will be billed as a monthly add-on and will show up on the invoice under "Data Bridge: temporary restore".

Next steps:
- Kimberly to send v0.4 DPA addendum (EOD Wed).
- Stephanie to share final sketch with HealthSync legal and confirm subprocessor list.
- HealthSync to confirm 60-day default or request 90-day default with rationale.
- If all agreed, Laura to issue an amendment and route to MedTechCo procurement for countersignature.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

(attachments: backup-retention-matrix.xlsx)
